clue.text: Professor on board joined dive

blocks.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in the board game Cluedo (Clue in the US)
met means came together, joined

explanation.surface: An academic sitting on a governing board took part in a plunge, perhaps a dive into the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' looks like membership of a committee, but the board is a games board: Cluedo's Professor Plum.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, so it is a verb synonym for dive.

clue.text: Term for Holy Father's yearly fast

blocks.note: p.a. is per annum, Latin for yearly
pacy means quick

explanation.surface: The Pope's annual period of fasting is given a name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'fast' a religious fast; it is the adjective for speedy, and 'Term' is a period in office, not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the period of office of a pope, the Holy Father.

clue.text: Weird alteration to the lunar year

indicators.note: an alteration changes something, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone finds a change to the lunar calendar decidedly odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthly means supernatural or eerie, a synonym for weird.

clue.text: Fly upside-down, possibly stupid

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning things upside-down means reading them from the bottom up

blocks.note: e.g., for example, marks something as one possibility
dim means slow-witted

explanation.surface: An insect flying upside-down might be a dim one.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a small two-winged insect, an example of a fly.

clue.text: Bucket Ted emptied behind tent, for personal use

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, leaving only its first and last letters
placed behind something means coming after it in the answer

blocks.note: a tipi is a conical tent
the outside letters of Ted
what is your own is for your personal use

explanation.surface: Ted empties a bucket behind his tent for his private needs, a camping latrine scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to bucket down is to rain very heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'bucket' and 'tip it down' are informal verbs for raining very hard.

clue.text: Clueless graduate ran after head of faculty

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
after places one piece later in the answer than another

blocks.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
the first letter of faculty
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: A hopeless graduate chased after the dean of the faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone baffled is perplexed, having no idea what is going on, much as clueless suggests.

clue.text: Eccentric saving crumbs

blocks.note: bar and saving both mean except, as in 'all bar one'
both crumbs and my are mild exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: An odd character who hoards the crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for crazy or daft, close to eccentric.

clue.text: Distressing fine justly deserved

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
what is rightful is justly due

explanation.surface: Someone upset at a fine they had to admit was fully deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful means dreadful or shocking, things that cause distress.

clue.text: Course along the coast learner marks with a pen

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
to ink is to mark with a pen

explanation.surface: A trainee walks a seaside route jotting notes with a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Links is a golf course on sandy ground by the sea.

clue.text: Indian calico made by underage weaving

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim note about child labour weaving cloth in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungaree was originally a coarse Indian cotton cloth, a kind of calico, before giving its name to overalls.

clue.text: Fraud returned subscriptions following pressure

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read in the opposite direction
following puts one piece after the other in the answer

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
membership dues are subscriptions

explanation.surface: A fraudster sent back members' subscriptions once they were pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious person faking intellectual depth, a kind of fraud.

clue.text: Place in France for every gourmand, and granny

blocks.note: per means for each
a pig is a greedy eater
nan is a familiar word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A French spot that suits every food lover and grandma too.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpignan is a city in southern France, near the Spanish border.

clue.text: Trade tote bags in prison

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: to tote is to carry
pent, as in pent up, means shut in or confined

explanation.surface: Inmates trading tote bags behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tote bags' reads as shopping bags; tote is the verb to carry and bags is the verb to capture.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is woodworking, a skilled craft or trade.

clue.text: What parasites live on a garden plant?

blocks.note: a parasite lives on its host
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders which plant pests feed on.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, hostas are notorious for being eaten by slugs and snails.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosta is a leafy shade plant common in gardens.

clue.text: Picture of horse-drawn vehicles in Jerusalem?

definitions.text: Picture of horse-drawn vehicles in Jerusalem?

blocks.clueFragment: Picture of horse-drawn vehicles in Jerusalem?
blocks.note: surface reading: an image of carts and carriages in the holy city

blocks.clueFragment: Picture of horse-drawn vehicles in Jerusalem?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a film whose title comes from a line in Blake's hymn Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A painting of carts and carriages in the streets of Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture means film; Blake's poem Jerusalem, sung as an English hymn, asks 'Bring me my chariot of fire', which gave the 1981 Oscar-winning athletics film its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The film is a motion picture named from the fiery war-vehicles in the hymn Jerusalem.

clue.text: Sailor nipped by insect gets something to lessen reaction

indicators.note: being nipped is being pinched between jaws, so one word sits gripped inside the other

blocks.note: a red ant is a stinging insect
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor bitten by a bug gets cream to calm the swelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an allergic reaction; the definition is about slowing a chemical one, as with fire retardant.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant is a substance that slows down a chemical process such as burning.

clue.text: Second team organised in style shown by diagram

indicators.note: organised things are put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside another word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
taken as written
chic is stylishness

explanation.surface: A reserve side set out stylishly, as a coach's tactics board shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Schematic describes something represented as a simplified diagram or plan.

clue.text: Rubber lining hotel bath that's broken before

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: an inn is a small hotel
a tub is a bath
ere is poetic for before

explanation.surface: A hotel bath had a rubber liner fitted after it cracked before.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner tube is the inflatable rubber ring lining the inside of some tyres.

clue.text: Fixing ropes are tied to is holding male climber

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a cleat is a fitting on a boat for securing ropes
M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's anchor point, where ropes are tied, secures a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rock climber; the climber is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant that scrambles up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Italy beaten then hung out to dry, to be frank

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
washing hung out to dry is on the washing line

explanation.surface: Italy lost and were then left exposed, frankly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hung out to dry' sounds like being abandoned after defeat; here it is literal laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay it on the line is an idiom meaning to speak plainly and bluntly.

clue.text: When did ship show the green light?

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to ship goods is to send them

explanation.surface: A query about when a vessel signalled a green light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' looks like a noun for a vessel; it is the verb to dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree or approve, giving permission, which is what a green light signals.

clue.text: Mr T has escaped from meanie

indicators.note: what has escaped is no longer there, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: Mr is short for mister
the letter itself

explanation.surface: Mr T, the A-Team actor, has got away from a nasty person.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is a stingy hoarder, and meanie is an informal word for a stingy person.

clue.text: Fly across lake in the sun

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching round it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to soar is to fly high
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A bird flies over a lake in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means of or relating to the sun, so solar energy is what lies in sunlight.

clue.text: Doctor who dreams, back from work, perhaps

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doctor Who dreams of heading home after a day's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D makes it look like the Time Lord of BBC television's Doctor Who; doctor is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Homewards means towards home, the direction taken coming back from work, among other places.

clue.text: Male on visit to hospital becomes Erica

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
at means present, visiting a place
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A man visiting hospital undergoes a change of identity to Erica.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name; it is the botanical genus of heathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Heath, or heather, is a plant of the genus Erica.

clue.text: Keep shaking from side to side in freight car

blocks.note: a dog's tail wags from side to side
on means continuing, as in 'keep on'

explanation.surface: Something keeps rocking about inside a railway goods truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a railway truck for carrying goods, a freight car.

clue.text: Separate friend leased back paintings

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the words are read right to left

blocks.note: pal is a friend
to let property is to lease it
paintings are works of art

explanation.surface: A friend who rented out a flat takes back their paintings separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell apart is to distinguish or separate one thing from another.

clue.text: Jumping muscle, excess energy

blocks.note: a glut is an excess supply
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A twitching muscle burns off surplus energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping' reads as twitching; it is the activity the muscle powers.
explanation.definitionFit: A glute is a buttock muscle, a major driver when leaping.

clue.text: Challenge boundaries in sexist gag

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of sexist
to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A comedian pushes limits with an offensive joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenge boundaries' wants to be one phrase; Challenge alone is the definition and boundaries picks letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is a demanding task that pushes someone beyond what is comfortable.

clue.text: Arrogance of Tory chair on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling is chosen by sound

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A Conservative chairman's haughtiness comes over in a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive pride in oneself, a synonym for arrogance.
